html:
On the 200 BCE map, Mon-Khmer covers much of mainland Southeast Asia, home to peoples speaking languages of the Austroasiatic family, the ancestors of the Mon, the Khmer and many hill peoples.

These languages probably spread with rice farmers who moved south into the region after about 2500 BCE. By 200 BCE villages in the river valleys of today's Thailand, Cambodia and Laos worked bronze and iron, as at Ban Chiang, and bronze drums of the Dong Son culture were traded widely.

Soon after, the first kingdoms appeared. Funan on the Mekong delta rose in the 1st century CE, and later the Mon kingdoms of Dvaravati and the Mon state of lower Burma. Khmer speakers built the Khmer Empire of Angkor. Not everyone in the region spoke these tongues: the Chams of Champa spoke an Austronesian language. Vietnamese and Khmer are the biggest Austroasiatic languages today.
sum: On the 200 BCE map, Mon-Khmer covers much of mainland Southeast Asia, home to peoples speaking languages of the Austroasiatic family, the ancestors of the Mon, the Khmer and many hill peoples.
